messages:
maria_devex: Heads-up — a few users hitting failures when installing the Python SDK from git: `pip install git+https://...`. Failure is on 3.10 and 3.11. Error snippet below:
```
ERROR: Could not build wheels for redwood-sdk, which is required to install pyproject.toml-based projects
```
Anyone familiar with our packaging state?

daniel_engineer: ugh. sounds like PEP 517 build backend or missing wheel in CI. Do we have a proper `pyproject.toml` with a build-backend listed?

sara_pkg: we do have pyproject, but historically our sdist didn't include `py.typed` and some stubs. poetry vs setuptools mismatch also caused editable/install-from-vcs problems.

leo_support: CI shows reproduce on linux-latest and macos-latest (arm64). link: https://ci.internal/runs/4023 (quick skim)

maria_devex: here's what a user pasted when they tried editable: `pip install -e .`
```
ERROR: Directory '.' is not installable. Neither 'pyproject.toml' nor 'setup.cfg' are present.
```
So weird — we do have pyproject.toml. Could be tooling version on their machine.

daniel_engineer: can you paste our pyproject build-system short block? I recall we had `poetry-core` at one point which requires `pip>=23` sometimes. If users have older pip it fails. Example: `build-system = {requires=["setuptools>=61","wheel"], build-backend="setuptools.build_meta"}`.

sara_pkg: agreed. Two concrete issues to check: 1) ensure `py.typed` is packaged (for typing consumers and to avoid mypy warnings), 2) include package data so any C-extensions/wheels are built on CI. For poetry users, recommend `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes -o requirements.txt` then `pip install -r requirements.txt` for reproducible installs.

ci-bot: Test failure: `packaging/test_install` failed on PR #1234 — wheel step errored. Logs: https://ci.internal/logs/1234

daniel_engineer: quick fix proposal — switch pyproject build-system to setuptools + wheel, add `py.typed` file next to package `redwood/py.typed` and update MANIFEST.in to include it. Also add `long_description_content_type = "text/markdown"` to setup metadata so `python -m build` works cleanly.

maria_devex: can someone paste the exact MANIFEST.in snippet? I'll add it to the PR.

sara_pkg: put this in MANIFEST.in:
```
include redwood/py.typed
recursive-include redwood/static *
```
And in setup.cfg (if using setuptools):
```
[options.packages.find]
where = src
include = redwood*

[options]
package_data =
    redwood: py.typed
```
If using poetry, set `include = [{"path": "redwood/py.typed"}]` in pyproject.

leo_support: note: M1 users reported pip trying to compile c-extensions and failing because no binary wheel on PyPI. Do we want to publish universal2 wheels?

daniel_engineer: yes for binary compatibility. Use `python -m build` on CI and twine upload; to build universal wheel add `zip_safe = False` and ensure any extension modules are optional or have wheel builds for platforms. For compiled deps, consider manylinux and macos universal2 builds via cibuildwheel.

maria_devex: side question — does this affect async client typing? Some users report `from redwood import AsyncClient` import errors after installing via poetry.

sara_pkg: that was probably because submodule `redwood.async_client` wasn't exposed in `__init__.py`. Packaging masked that since editable local installs worked for devs but sdist omitted it. Add `__all__` export or import in package `__init__.py`: `from .async_client import AsyncClient` so `from redwood import AsyncClient` works.

leo_support: can we add a short repro in docs for both pip and poetry workflows? I can add a support KB: steps to reproduce + temp workaround (use `pip install -e .` after `poetry build` or `poetry export`).

maria_devex: SG. I'll open a small PR with these three changes: pyproject build-system -> setuptools+wheel, include py.typed, export async client in __init__.py. CI-bot can we re-run tests after that?

ci-bot: Manual re-run requested for PR #1234 queued.

daniel_engineer: thanks — if anyone runs into edge-case with old pip: advise `python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel build` first.

sara_pkg: also adding a note in CONTRIBUTING.md about reproducible builds: `python -m build` then `pip install dist/redwood-*.whl` is the supported path for releases. For developers using poetry, add `poetry export` snippet.

maria_devex: perfect. I'll paste the PR link when it's up. Thanks all :rocket:
